primary_claim: In Qwen3.6-27B, J-lens surfaces 'meta-tokens' (e.g. disambiguation tokens like 什么意思, the 'gcd' token on LCM problems, the hedging token 大概率) that give causal evidence of the algorithm or process the model is using, even when the J-lens vector itself is not causal, as shown by negative steering and swap experiments that change the model's disambiguation, arithmetic, and hedging behavior.

effect.metric: rate of committing to a single answer under negative steering of the hedging meta-token vs baseline/random-steering
effect.value: baseline commits to single answer <12% of the time on the highest prompt; negative steering on the hedging meta-token significantly increases this rate, while random-vector steering has little to no effect

contradicts_or_qualifies: extends Gurnee et al.'s finding that most J-space tokens relate directly to next-token prediction by showing that some meta-tokens more directly indicate the algorithm used rather than just intermediate variables
stated_future_work: build multi-token J-lens methods to surface meta-concepts that are not lexicalized as a single token
investigate the 'stack' and 'xor' meta-token candidates found on parenthesis-balancing and repeat-finding tasks
leave a complete account of whether such tokens are learned associations or actual algorithms to future work
build off the current work on meta-tokens toward further progress on algorithm interpretability
limitations_stated: scope of the study is limited to single-token (mostly Chinese-phrase) meta-tokens in one 27B model
the J-lens vector itself is often not causal; ablating the meta-token direction generally had no effect, only negative steering did
the autoresearch loop for finding meta-tokens surfaced fewer non-obvious survivors than hoped, likely because J-lens is bounded by computations lexicalized as a single vocabulary token
'stack' and 'xor' meta-token candidates were noted but not investigated deeply
quote: Negative steering with the interpretative meta-token consistently decreased the model’s recognition of the prompt context
